hot.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
Looped World Models
hot.summary: LoopWM introduces the first looped transformer architecture for world modeling, leveraging iterative latent depth to achieve stable long-horizon simulations with high parameter efficiency. The model demonstrates superior predictive accuracy and reduced computational cost on benchmarks like ScienceWorld and AlfWorld, outperforming models up to 100 times larger.

hot.title: VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models
hot.summary: VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion-parameter model from Sina Weibo Inc., achieves advanced verifiable reasoning capabilities, matching or exceeding the performance of significantly larger language models on demanding benchmarks in mathematics, coding, and scientific reasoning. The model scored 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, further improving to 97.1 on AIME26 and 99.2 on BruMO25 with Claim-Level Reliability Assessment.

hot.title: Variable-Width Transformers
You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences
hot.summary: Researchers from UIUC and NYU propose Temporal Difference in Vision (TDV), a self-supervised method for learning visual representations from video by predicting future frame embeddings from past frames and learned motion. This approach, which avoids strong inductive biases, demonstrates improved performance on dense spatial tasks like optical flow and stereo depth compared to existing techniques like DINO and iBOT.

hot.title: Latent Thought Flow: Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
hot.summary: Latent Thought Flow (LTF), developed by researchers at Singapore Management University and Ant Group, enables Large Language Models to perform adaptive, efficient multi-step reasoning directly within their continuous latent space. The framework, which leverages GFlowNets, achieved an average accuracy improvement of 9.5% and a 27.2% reduction in reasoning length compared to existing latent reasoning methods across various LLM backbones and benchmarks.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotWorld introduces a language-conditioned video world model from the Qwen Team that unifies various embodied domains, including manipulation, driving, and navigation, using natural language as a singular action interface. The model predicts physically plausible future visual trajectories and demonstrates top performance on embodied intelligence benchmarks like EWMBench and DreamGen Bench.

hot.title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training
hot.summary: ExpRL, developed by researchers from Stanford University, Carnegie Mellon University, and OpenAI, introduces an on-policy reinforcement learning approach for mid-training large language models by using human-written reference solutions as dense reward scaffolds. This method improves the initial policy for subsequent sparse-reward RL, leading to enhanced reasoning capabilities and achieving 63.41% pass@1 on AIME-2026 after downstream training, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and sparse reward baselines.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotManip, a Vision-Language-Action foundation model, demonstrates that aligning heterogeneous robotic data enables effective data scaling and emergent generalization capabilities for manipulation tasks. The model achieves robust performance across various out-of-distribution scenarios and real-world deployments by integrating a unified cross-embodiment formulation and a large-scale open-source pretraining corpus.

hot.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos
hot.summary: The DO AS I DO algorithm generates dexterous manipulation data for multi-fingered robots by reconstructing 3D hand-object interactions from everyday monocular human videos and retargeting them into executable robot actions. This approach achieved a 71% success rate on reconstructed in-the-wild trajectories and demonstrated real-world execution across diverse tasks.

hot.title: DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model
hot.summary: The DreamX Team developed DreamX-World 1.0, a general-purpose interactive world model that transitions video generation from passive synthesis to dynamic, user-controlled simulation. This model achieved the highest overall scores in basic (84.76) and long-horizon (70.41) evaluations against larger competitors, and was preferred by humans in 57.5-61.9% of cases, while also demonstrating enhanced scene persistence and real-time streaming at up to 16 FPS.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System
Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
hot.summary: The Geometric Action Model (GAM) repurposes a pretrained Geometric Foundation Model (GFM) as a unified backbone for language-conditioned robot manipulation, integrating 3D perception, future geometry prediction, and action decoding. This approach improves policy robustness to environmental changes and achieves significantly faster inference speeds, up to 55 times quicker than diffusion-based baselines.

hot.title: From AGI to ASI
hot.summary: Researchers at Google DeepMind establish an analytical framework to map the potential evolution of artificial intelligence from AGI to ASI, outlining four technological pathways and six specific bottlenecks. The work provides a research agenda for predicting and managing the development of advanced AI capabilities.

hot.title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
hot.summary: Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM), developed by researchers at ELLIS Institute Tübingen and ETH Zurich, present a looped transformer architecture designed for stable and adaptive reasoning. The model incorporates a fixed-point convergence mechanism for intrinsic halting and utilizes pre-normalization with residual scaling to manage signal propagation in deep effective layers, achieving competitive or superior performance on various puzzle tasks while adaptively allocating computation based on task complexity.

hot.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction
hot.summary: The Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington developed MolmoMotion, a system that forecasts object-attached 3D point trajectories in world coordinates, conditioned on language instructions and visual history. This method improved robot manipulation task success rates by over 20 percentage points and enhanced video generation realism, outperforming existing motion prediction baselines on a new 3D motion benchmark.

hot.title: Zone of Proximal Policy Optimization: Teacher in Prompts, Not Gradients
hot.summary: Zone of Proximal Policy Optimization (ZPPO) enables smaller language and vision-language models to leverage teacher knowledge through prompt reformulations, enhancing broad generalization and learning on challenging questions where traditional reinforcement learning fails, outperforming distillation and standard PPO methods.

hot.title: Learning from the Self-future: On-policy Self-distillation for dLLMs
hot.summary: d-OPSD introduces the first on-policy self-distillation framework tailored for diffusion large language models, leveraging 'self future-experience' and step-level divergence supervision to enable self-improvement. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in reasoning tasks while demonstrating superior sample efficiency, converging in approximately 10% of the optimization steps required by RLVR methods.

hot.title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding
hot.summary: OmniAgent, a framework for multimodal large language models, enables scalable understanding of long-form videos by reformulating perception as an iterative reasoning process, distilling transient multimodal data into a persistent textual memory. It sets new state-of-the-art recall accuracy across ten omni-modal benchmarks, including a 50.5% accuracy on LVBench, while demonstrating greater efficiency by using significantly fewer frames than larger passive models.

hot.title: Guava: An Effective and Universal Harness for Embodied Manipulation
hot.summary: The Guava framework enables compact, open-source language models to achieve robust, generalizable robotic manipulation by employing iterative reasoning, semantic action abstractions, and multimodal observations. The 4-billion parameter Guava-Agent-4B attained 75.6% overall success in simulation and strong zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, often surpassing larger proprietary models while demonstrating emergent failure recovery.

HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry

It enables agents to systematically learn and improve their runtime interfaces from execution feedback, including co-evolving with the underlying language model to internalize new strategies.

likes.summary: HyVLA-0.5, a comprehensive robot learning stack from Tencent Robotics X and Tencent Hy Team, unifies high-fidelity data collection, VLM-based training, preference-driven policy refinement, and real-world deployment for generalist robots. The system achieved 90.9% success on clean simulated tasks and demonstrated effective cross-embodiment transfer and robust policy improvement via reward-free post-training on real robots.

likes.summary: RepFusion introduces a text-to-image (T2I) generation framework that leverages a frozen, pretrained Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) to actively denoise in representation space by dynamically processing evolving noisy visual representations. This method enhances T2I performance and achieves parameter efficiency by utilizing the MLLM's strong multimodal priors for adaptive conditioning.

likes.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
likes.summary: LaWAM (Latent World Action Models) proposes an approach for dynamics-aware robot policies that efficiently predict compact latent visual subgoals, rather than high-dimensional pixel-level future observations. This method enables robots to anticipate action consequences with significantly reduced inference latency and model complexity compared to traditional pixel-space world models, achieving high success rates across diverse manipulation tasks.

likes.title: Variable-Width Transformers
T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
likes.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley, NVIDIA, Stanford, and other institutions developed the T-Rex framework, enabling Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to incorporate high-frequency tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation. This approach achieved an average success rate of 65% across 12 contact-rich tasks, outperforming the strongest baseline by more than 30%.

likes.title: Gaze Heads: How VLMs Look at What They Describe
likes.summary: Gandikota and Bau identify "gaze heads" in vision-language models, a specific subset of attention heads that dynamically focus on image regions as the model generates descriptive text. Intervening on these heads causally steers the model's visual grounding with up to 83.1% redirection accuracy, and this mechanism generalizes across various VLM architectures but is largely absent in models with frozen vision encoders.

likes.title: VisualClaw: A Real-Time, Personalized Agent for the Physical World
likes.summary: VisualClaw is a multimodal agent framework that utilizes an edge-side cascaded encoding gate for efficient video processing and a self-evolving skill and memory bank for continual adaptation. It introduces VisualClawArena, a new benchmark for evaluating agents in tool-using, workspace-centric scenarios, demonstrating improved accuracy while significantly reducing VLM API costs by an average of 98.1% compared to full-frame video input.
